text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.6% today, but this modest move masks a brutal two-week slide of nearly 10% that accelerated sharply starting November 4th. The stock has been dragged down by falling oil prices—US crude dropped to $99.64 per barrel today, well below the $154 level when the decline began. Oil refiners and producers like ConocoPhillips are directly exposed to crude prices, so when crude falls this hard, their profits and valuations compress quickly, regardless of company-specific news.

The recent earnings report and SEC filings released on November 5th haven't stopped the selling pressure. Investors appear more focused on the near-term direction of oil prices, which have become volatile around geopolitical risk: midterm election results on November 5th reduced immediate fears of Iran conflict escalation, allowing prices to slide, though some analysts still expect crude could spike back above $100 if tensions reignite. With crude still near a multi-week low, the pressure on energy stocks persists.
